primaryMetrics.M2: integrated Merkle snapshot root and target-path construction

interpretationGuardrails: N is occupied eligible-set size; configured Merkle depth remains 17 for every profile.
M1 and M2 are the stages whose work directly incorporates the controlled eligible-set population.
M2 is an integrated snapshot/root/target-path construction metric; no isolated path-extraction timing claim is made.
M3, M4, and M5 use the same fixed-depth circuit and frozen proving artifacts for every N.
Observed M3-M5 runtime differences are descriptive runtime variation and are not interpreted as N-dependent circuit-complexity changes.
Pilot observations and warmups are excluded from final statistics.
No measured observations are removed as outliers.
No causal opcode-cost claim is made.
No on-chain eligible-set scaling claim is made.
Local cryptographic-stage latency is not directly compared with previously published biometric/IoT end-to-end voting latency.
publicationSafeConclusions: Across the tested profiles, occupied eligible-set size N was varied from 10 to 10000 while Merkle depth remained fixed at 17.
The measured off-chain eligible-set preparation stages M1 and M2 showed monotonically increasing mean runtime across the tested N levels.

Witness generation, Groth16 proving, and Groth16 verification were measured under the same fixed-depth circuit and frozen proving artifacts; their observed runtime variation is reported descriptively rather than as eligible-set-dependent circuit-complexity scaling.
These results characterize the tested local off-chain cryptographic pipeline and do not constitute an on-chain eligible-set scaling benchmark.
